memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"They served as judges for the people at all times. The difficult cases they
brought to Moses, but the simple ones they decided themselves. Then Moses sent
his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro returned to his own country."
- Ex 18:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The system works. It becomes normal life: judges serving at all times, difficult
cases going up, simple ones handled locally.

And then Jethro goes home.

There is something quietly moving about that. He came, he saw what was needed,
he said what had to be said, and he left. He did not stay to supervise the
implementation or make sure he received credit. He did not attach himself to
Israel's story.

Some of the most valuable people in our lives are like this. They arrive at the
right moment, say one true thing, and move on. They are not permanent fixtures.
Their contribution is brief and enormous.

And some of us are called to be that person for someone else. Not everyone we
help becomes a long-term relationship. Sometimes faithfulness means offering
what we have and then stepping back.

Notice that the chapter ends without fanfare. Jethro returned to his own country.
No monument, no title. But Israel's entire system of justice, later formalised in
Deuteronomy, began with one visitor asking a good question.

You never know which conversation will outlast you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who came into your life briefly and changed its direction?
2. Are you willing to help without needing to stay involved?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to give what I have to give and then step back gladly. Thank You
for those who did that for me. Amen.
